CAPTURE-007.summary: Capture erasure retains anonymous replay proofs and private archive matching contexts.
CAPTURE-007.was: Captured evidence, proposals and source state are part of every export and restore under DATA-001; source credentials never are, so a restored provider source must be reconnected. Erasing a contact erases the captured evidence and proposals that carry them under DATA-002, and the audit trail keeps only their count.
CAPTURE-007.now: Captured evidence, proposals and source state are part of every export and restore under DATA-001; source credentials never are, so a restored provider source must be reconnected. Erasing a contact erases the captured evidence and proposals that carry them under DATA-002. The audit trail keeps counts and anonymous keyed replay proofs with erasure times, without addresses, original item identifiers or content, so later intake cannot recreate erased originals. Private matching contexts and proofs travel in archives; restoring an owner's historical archive retains DATA-001's existing behavior.

BRIEF-001.summary: The top of the operator home is a brief built from records only, so it works with the AI provider unconfigured (AI-003). Per account (the company when one is known, otherwise the opportunity, otherwise the contact) it lists the customer signals linked since the operator last marked the brief seen, or, before they ever have, over the stale interval counted from the start of the day (UTC), with replies and booked, completed or cancelled meetings first and observed signals kept apart from inferred ones (SIGNAL-006); the account's overdue promises (BRIEF-002); and application handoffs waiting for review (BRIEF-005). Signals that match no record and replies without thread headers are listed as unresolved identity, never guessed; captured replies and meetings waiting for a person to accept or decline their proposed link are listed as held for capture review. Every line shows its occurred time and links to the record, timeline entry, draft, task or review item it rests on; a line without such evidence is not shown. Marking the brief seen records the operator and the time the brief was built in the audit trail, so anything arriving later stays new. A day with nothing says so. The brief is for full native operators; invited collaborators cannot read it.

BRIEF-002.summary: Computed from records when the brief is built: an open internal next action (a handoff task a person wrote or accepted) or an open opportunity's next action past its due time; the latest customer reply on a record with no approved outbound message, captured sent message, logged call or meeting, or completed action on that record since, once the awaiting-response interval (TEAM-003, working days in the workspace timezone) has passed; a meeting completed within the last 120 days with no note, logged call or meeting, completed action, handoff, draft, approved message or captured sent message on its records after it; and a draft on an open opportunity with no outbound message other than a cancelled one. A recommendation carries no due time and is never a promise by itself.

BRIEF-003.summary: With a provider configured (AI-001), an operator can ask for a one-paragraph summary of one account's brief lines. The request preview shows every field sent, and the request is sent only unchanged from that preview; a brief that changed since the preview is refused with 409. Output must validate and cite only evidence IDs from that account's lines (AI-002); failing or uncited output is recorded (AI-004) and shown as failed, never repaired or replaced. Summaries are not stored, and a provider failure leaves the brief whole.

BRIEF-004.summary: A meeting signal linked to a record (booked, completed or cancelled, from a source or from capture) has a plan page: its time exactly as the source gave it or the statement that none was given; attendees resolved by exact email key (RECORD-003) with their company and open opportunities; attendees with no record listed as unresolved, never guessed, with a way to create a contact with that exact address; the opportunities with value, stage and owner and their total open value; the last interactions on its records and the outstanding promises on them (BRIEF-002), each citing its timeline entry or record. The agenda and prep notes are saved as one note under RECORD-010 on the meeting's opportunity (or its company or contact) and edited in place. A person can turn a cited plan line into an internal next action on the meeting's opportunity that cites that line. Planning creates no draft and sends nothing (OUT-001).

BRIEF-005.summary: Within the scoped application delegation below and with no new scope: `crm.evidence.read` also reads the brief, narrowed to lines resting on selected records, and the plan of a meeting that is selected or linked to a selected record, narrowed to the selected records and the contacts and company of selected opportunities; a line or interaction resting only on opportunities outside the grant is left out even when it shares a contact or company, records outside the grant are left off the lines shown, and unresolved attendees show only their address. A line seen only through a signal selected by id keeps only selected records; one left with none is listed apart from the accounts and links to that signal's evidence read. A held line names a proposed contact or company only when it is selected, and a selected contact's line is filed under its company only when that company is selected too. `orbit.handoff.upsert` content may cite evidence IDs; each must be a signal, timeline entry, draft or task on that opportunity, its contacts or its company, or the write is refused with 422. A handoff an application wrote is a proposal, shown in the brief and on the opportunity with its cited evidence (or the statement that it cites none), until a person accepts it, saves an edited version or dismisses it; that review appends one timeline entry attributed to the person and naming the application. No handoff can approve or start a message (OUT-001). Without consent, without the write scope or after revocation an application cannot write, and revocation stops its reads at once.

PUBLIC-004.summary: Native sign-in declares its path, brand and theme in src/identity.ts; authentication requirements are unchanged.
PUBLIC-004.was: Base operator-auth over Orbit's own operators: configured email-link delivery sends only to an existing active operator, gives the same request response for unknown and inactive addresses, and exchanges a hashed, single-use link, confirmed by POST from a read-only confirmation page within 15 minutes, for a secure native session. An optional linked identity provider (an Auth install) admits only existing operators and stays off until the owner turns it on. Return locations stay inside the operator app. Sign-out revokes that session. A missing or failed mail configuration cannot issue a session.
PUBLIC-004.now: Base operator-auth over Orbit's own operators: configured email-link delivery sends only to an existing active operator, gives the same request response for unknown and inactive addresses, and exchanges a hashed, single-use link, confirmed by POST from a read-only confirmation page within 15 minutes, for a secure native session. An optional linked identity provider (an Auth install) admits only existing operators and stays off until the owner turns it on. Return locations stay inside the operator app. Sign-out revokes that session. A missing or failed mail configuration cannot issue a session. Orbit’s sign-in path, brand and theme are declared in `src/identity.ts`.

proseChanges.summary: Documents the packaged rer CLI, read-only Google/Microsoft capture setup, Today brief, and local versus hosted backup procedures; adds demo media.
proseChanges.was: Local commands used node scripts/rer.mjs; capture documented file intake and future provider adapters.
proseChanges.now: Commands use the pinned @runeditrun/rer CLI; Google and Microsoft capture require the owner's OAuth client and live-account proof remains in OWNER-STEPS.md. Today brief and meeting plans are documented. Local .rer archives and hosted Records JSON archives use separate transfer paths.

proseChanges.summary: Use the pinned packaged rer CLI and Orbit installer; hosted transfers use explicit remote origin and private session file.
proseChanges.was: Local operations ran node scripts/rer.mjs through the repository wrapper.
proseChanges.now: @runeditrun/rer is pinned exactly; local operations use rer with scripts/installer/local.mjs. Hosted Records transfer adds --target remote --origin HTTPS_ORIGIN --session-file FILE. Preserve native operator identity and applied migration bytes.

extensionPointChanges.summary: The existing capture.source.v1 contract is now listed in seed.json extensionPoints.adapters and implemented for scoped read-only Google and Microsoft connections alongside file intake; it grants no outreach authority.

migrations.buyerSteps: Take a verified backup and stop intake and writes before rer setup (local) or the separately authorized deployment applies this new migration. It adds installation-local capture_oauth and capture_locks tables and their indexes without replacing prior tables or sending messages. Preserve all already-applied migration bytes. Existing file capture needs no provider connection; provider capture requires the owner's OAuth client, ORBIT_ENCRYPTION_KEY and explicit read-only scope selection.

agentUpdateInstructions: Update from v0.1.0 without resetting or replacing installation state. Save a verified backup outside the checkout, preserve native operators, setup identity, records, files, queues, owner changes and every applied migration byte; stop dev/preview, writes, scheduled processing and source intake before updating. Install frozen dependencies with Node 22.20.0 and pnpm 10.12.4; local rer setup applies only pending migration 0036_capture_providers.sql and keeps the existing owner and settings. Verify records and outbound states before resuming; never replay sends. Use MIGRATION-RECOVERY.md for the distinct local and hosted backup/restore paths, including credentials and authority excluded from archives. Configure or reconnect provider sources separately with the owner's OAuth client and encryption key. The Today brief and meeting plans add no sending authority; existing delegation scopes and handoffs without citations remain valid. rer is pinned at 0.2.4. This release adds no capacity promise and claims no live Google/Microsoft account, mail delivery, hosted application deployment or inbound-mail acceptance.
